title: CBS Radio Mystery Theater
paragraphs: Himan Brown's hour-long dramatic anthology revived radio mystery for a later generation with stories of crime, horror, the supernatural, science fiction, and suspense, most famously hosted by E. G. Marshall.

Himan Brown’s CBS dramatic anthology revived network radio drama in 1974. The archive distinguishes 1,399 numbered original programs from later repeat broadcasts. The frozen GRH snapshot contains 1,429 playable objects representing 1,354 distinct episode numbers plus 75 additional copies/variants; 45 numbered originals are absent from this snapshot.

GRH documents the program through E. G. Marshall host era (January 6, 1974 to January 29, 1982) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] and Tammy Grimes final host era (February 1, 1982 to December 7, 1982) on [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are E. G. Marshall (host on 710 recordings and performer on 2 recordings), Himan Brown (director on 697 recordings, producer on 695 recordings, and host on 1 recording), Ian Martin (performer on 151 recordings, writer on 138 recordings, and radio adaptor on 24 recordings), Sam Dann (writer on 190 recordings, radio adaptor on 23 recordings, author on 1 recording, and performer on 1 recording), Robert Dryden (performer on 179 recordings), Bryna Raeburn (performer on 136 recordings), and Marian Seldes (performer on 125 recordings).
The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] (broadcast on network).
Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Murder, Supernatural phenomena, War and military conflict, Medicine and psychology, Occult and curses, and Trials and legal process.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including Network radio drama revival in the television era, Sponsor-supported national radio drama in the 1970s, and Golden-age radio veterans alongside newer stage and screen actors.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|theater-five|Theater Five]] (69 shared credited people), [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (50 shared credited people), [[show|x-minus-one|X Minus One]] (48 shared credited people), [[show|columbia-workshop|Columbia Workshop]] (48 shared credited people), and [[show|the-chase|The Chase]] (33 shared credited people).
